globals.detail: Wire: reads and commands for dashboards made from the myGrenton interface. The Grenton page writes the dashboards as plain Dashboard code (#220); what reads a CLU or sends it a command goes through these helpers, so it never waits for the CLU and is checked: s:toggle("w2", "Hall light", nil, Wire.isOn(Wire.value("CLU221000002.DOU0001")), Wire.onOff(Wire.set("CLU221000002.DOU0001", 0, 1), Wire.set("CLU221000002.DOU0001", 0, 0))) s:status("w4", "Setpoint", nil, Wire.variable("CLU221000002", "setpoint"), "°C") s:slider("w9", "Dimmer", 0, 100, Wire.percent(Wire.value("CLU221000002.DIM0001")), Wire.fromPercent(Wire.set("CLU221000002.DIM0001", 0, Wire.INPUT))) s:button("w7", "Evening", nil, Wire.script("CLU221000002", "setup", "evening", 2)) A path is "<CLU>.<object>" as the registry has it, or "<CLU>" for the CLU's own features; an object the registry does not have is neither read nor commanded. What the registry follows (the value of an object on the Sync list) is read from it; anything else is asked in the background, at most Wire.perCLU at a time, and the widget shows the last answer. The CLU only forwards the panel's events (click(name, input)); this library keeps the state (open pages, cursor, edits, idle timer) and draws the screen with frames sent by RemotePanel. globals.label: tasmota
globals.detail: Tasmota devices over MQTT: a device is one line in a module. The library creates objects bound to the device; expose stays in the module. local tasmota = require("lib/tasmota") local lamp = tasmota.switch("tasmota_75088A")            -- { relay = 2 } for POWER2 expose(lamp, "light", { path = "tasmota.biurko", name = "Lampka biurko", area = "Biuro" }) The topic is the device's Topic (Configuration -> MQTT). State comes from stat/<topic>/POWER<n>, RESULT and tele/<topic>/STATE, sensors from tele/<topic>/SENSOR; commands go to cmnd/<topic>/... A state from the device is never sent back as a command. The state is asked for on start, when the MQTT client connects and when the device comes back (LWT Online). A change from the device is recorded with the device as the actor (device:<topic>). The library subscribes stat/<topic>/+ and tele/<topic>/+; MQTT keeps one callback per pattern, so a module must not subscribe those patterns itself (subscribe e.g. tele/<topic>/SENSOR). It needs the default client without a topic prefix, and the device's Full Topic as Tasmota sets it (%prefix%/%topic%/). Used so far with a Sonoff Basic only (one relay); relays 2+, the dimmer and sensors follow Tasmota's documented messages, untried on a device.
globals.documentation: Tasmota devices over MQTT: a device is one line in a module. The library creates objects bound to the device; expose stays in the module. local tasmota = require("lib/tasmota") local lamp = tasmota.switch("tasmota_75088A")            -- { relay = 2 } for POWER2 expose(lamp, "light", { path = "tasmota.biurko", name = "Lampka biurko", area = "Biuro" }) The topic is the device's Topic (Configuration -> MQTT). State comes from stat/<topic>/POWER<n>, RESULT and tele/<topic>/STATE, sensors from tele/<topic>/SENSOR; commands go to cmnd/<topic>/... A state from the device is never sent back as a command. The state is asked for on start, when the MQTT client connects and when the device comes back (LWT Online). A change from the device is recorded with the device as the actor (device:<topic>). The library subscribes stat/<topic>/+ and tele/<topic>/+; MQTT keeps one callback per pattern, so a module must not subscribe those patterns itself (subscribe e.g. tele/<topic>/SENSOR). It needs the default client without a topic prefix, and the device's Full Topic as Tasmota sets it (%prefix%/%topic%/). Used so far with a Sonoff Basic only (one relay); relays 2+, the dimmer and sensors follow Tasmota's documented messages, untried on a device.

globals.label: cct
globals.detail: Tunable white from two dimmers: a warm and a cold white channel as one colour temperature. local cct = require("lib/cct") local biuro = cct.mix(_:get("CLU1.DIM1"), _:get("CLU1.DIM2"), { warm = 2700, cold = 6500 }) dash:section("Biuro"):colorTemp("biuro", "Biuro", biuro, { min = 2700, max = 6500 }) A channel is anything with getValue/setValue on 0..1 (RemoteLight, RemoteLedChannel, VirtualDimmer). Brightness is the sum of both channels (at most 100%), the colour temperature their ratio, linear in kelvin between warm and cold. Changing one keeps the other. A colour temperature set while both are off is kept for the next switchOn, and so are the level and colour temperature a light had before it was switched off (also by a scene or a wall switch, when a poll saw them). While the channels show what the mix sent (within one 0..255 step) it keeps its own kelvin: a dim light on stepped channels does not drift. Commands go out at least 50 ms apart, only the latest values wait: the CLU drops bursts (pkg/lua/AGENTS.md).

globals.label: Cloud
globals.detail: Cloud - notifications to the members' phones through vclu cloud. Cloud.notify("Pralka skończyła") Cloud.notify{ title = "Alarm!", body = "Strefa 2: ruch", priority = "high", to = "admins", tag = "alarm", open = "alarm", actions = { { label = "Rozbrój", roles = { "admin" }, run = function(who) Satel.partition(1):disarm(); return "Rozbrojono (" .. who.name .. ")" end }, { label = "Otwórz bramę", run = function() BRAMA:execute(0) end }, } } Calendar.new('dom'):notify(Cloud.channel{ to = "all" }) Cloud.onPresence(function(e) if not e.anyone then Satel.partition(1):arm() end      -- the last one left if e.home and e.name == "Anna" then SALON_LAMPA:switchOn() end end) if Cloud.anyoneHome() then ... end Cloud.disable(); Cloud.enable(); if Cloud.enabled() then ... end vCLU sends the notification to the cloud, which picks the people (to) and sends a push to their phones; the cloud never sees the buttons' code, only their labels. A pressed button comes back with who pressed it, and its run(who) runs here, as that person (origin "remote", actor "cloud:<id>" in history). While the cloud is unreachable notifications wait up to 10 minutes. Buttons work for `expires` seconds (default 1 h, at most 24 h) and until a Lua reload. The cloud limits a home to 5 notifications a minute and 30 an hour. Presence comes from the members' phones: each person who turned it on in the app is "home" or "away" (a geofence on the phone; the cloud never learns where the home or the phone is). A change of someone known calls the onPresence handlers, as that person (origin "remote"); the first list after vCLU starts, and someone starting or stopping to share, only set the state.

globals.detail: Persist - automation state that survives a Lua reload and a restart. local st = persist("wiatrolap", { pauseUntil = 0 }) st.pauseUntil = os.time() + 600   -- saved to KV a moment later (debounced) The returned table is an empty proxy over hidden data, so every assignment (also to an existing key) goes through __newindex and is saved. V1 keeps a flat map of JSON-serializable values: replace a nested table as a whole, or call st:save() after mutating it. Methods: get, set, save, toTable (gopher-lua has no __pairs); these names are reserved keys. Data lives in KV namespace "module:<name>", key "state". Persist.flushAll() writes pending changes; Go calls it before a reload and at shutdown.

Only FEATURE_TIME and FEATURE_MODE can be set; other features are read-only. timer:set(Timer.FEATURE_TIME, 10000)  -- Set timer to 10 seconds timer:set(Timer.FEATURE_MODE, Timer.MODE_COUNT_DOWN)  -- Set to countdown mode

Timer.documentation: Get a timer feature value Retrieves current timer properties including time, mode, state, and remaining value. All features can be read, though only FEATURE_TIME and FEATURE_MODE can be modified via set(). local timeRemaining = timer:get(Timer.FEATURE_VALUE) local currentState = timer:get(Timer.FEATURE_STATE) if currentState == Timer.STATE_COUNTING then print("Timer is running, " .. timeRemaining .. Timer.label: execute
Timer.documentation: Execute a timer method Controls timer operation by executing start, stop, or pause commands. This is the primary interface for controlling timer execution state. timer:execute(Timer.METHOD_START)   -- Start/resume the timer timer:execute(Timer.METHOD_PAUSE)   -- Pause the timer timer:execute(Timer.METHOD_STOP)    -- Stop the timer completely

Builder.documentation: Register the calendar and start it. Replaces a calendar with the same id. @api public

Cal.label: on
Cal.documentation: Subscribe: on(kind, fn) or on(kind, id, fn); kinds start, end, reminder, change, ready. At one moment end comes before start; an end from skip, pause or remove has e.cancelled = true.

Cal.label: day
Cal.documentation: A day: { date, weekday ('mo'..'su'), workday, holiday, holidayName, namedays, starts, ends }; date as 'YYYY-MM-DD' or a timestamp, today when nil. Names follow :holidays(country). @api public

Cal.label: between
Cal.documentation: Occurrences between two moments (timestamps, or dates: from its start, to its end), also the ones going on at from; at most 400 days. opts: { tags }. @api public

Cal.label: today
Cal.documentation: Occurrences of today (also the ones that started earlier and still go on). @api public

Cal.label: upcoming
Cal.documentation: Occurrences from now for the next n days (default 7). @api public

Cal.label: next
Cal.documentation: The next occurrence of an event (not skipped), or nil. @api public

Cal.label: isActive
Cal.documentation: Whether an occurrence of the event is going on now (nil until the clock is trusted). @api public

Cal.label: value
Cal.documentation: The value of a schedule now (nil until the clock is trusted). @api public

Cal.label: nextChange
Cal.documentation: The next change of a schedule within 8 days: { value, at } or nil. @api public

Cal.label: color
Cal.documentation: The colour given to a value of a schedule (default: its value now), or nil. @api public

Cal.label: segments
Cal.documentation: Spans of a schedule: segments(id, from, to) with timestamps or dates, or segments(id, date) for one day: { {from, to, value, color}, ... }. @api public

Cal.label: sun
Cal.documentation: Sunrise, sunset, civil dawn and dusk, and solar noon of a day (date, timestamp or today), or nil without :location(). { sunrise, sunset, dawn, dusk, noon, dayLength } as timestamps; polar = 'day' | 'night' when the sun does not rise or set. @api public

Cal.label: sunPosition
Cal.documentation: Where the sun is now (or at a timestamp): { azimuth (degrees from north, 180 south), elevation (degrees above the horizon) }, or nil without :location(). @api public

Cal.label: isDay
Cal.documentation: Whether it is day now (or at a timestamp): between :daylight()'s from and to, by the sun with :location(), else by the fallback hours. Nil until the clock is trusted. @api public

Cal.label: isNight
Cal.documentation: The opposite of isDay(at); nil until the clock is trusted. @api public

Cal.label: isWorkday
Cal.documentation: Whether a date ('YYYY-MM-DD', a timestamp or today) is a workday. @api public

Cal.label: isHoliday
Cal.documentation: Whether a date is a public holiday. @api public

Cal.label: isReady
Cal.documentation: Whether the clock is trusted and the calendar fires events. @api public

Cal.label: add
Cal.documentation: Add a user event (saved, survives a restart). Fields as in :event without functions.

Cal.label: remove
Cal.documentation: Remove a user event. @api public

Cal.label: skip
Cal.documentation: Cancel one occurrence of an event (by its date). @api public

Cal.label: unskip
Cal.documentation: Undo skip(). @api public

Cal.label: pause
Cal.documentation: Pause events in a range of days: pause('2026-12-24..2027-01-02', { tags = {'dzieci'} }). @api public

Cal.label: resume
Cal.documentation: Remove all pauses. @api public

Cal.label: paused
Cal.documentation: Pauses not over yet: { {from, to, tags}, ... }. @api public

Cal.label: info
Cal.documentation: State for MCP and the panel: ready, reason, events, schedules. @api public

Calendar.label: get
Calendar.documentation: A calendar built with Calendar.new(id):build(), or nil. @api public

Calendar.label: list
Calendar.documentation: All calendars in the order they were built. @api public

Camera.label: register
Camera.documentation: Register a camera for snapshot proxy. url      (string) Full URL to camera snapshot endpoint auth     (string) Auth type: "digest", "basic", or nil for none username (string) Username for auth password (string) Password for auth

Camera.label: snapshotUrl
Camera.documentation: Get the snapshot URL for a registered camera.

Cloud.label: notify
Cloud.documentation: Sends a notification to the members' phones. opts: title (required), body, priority ("normal" or "high"), to ("all", "admins" or a list of cloud ids), tag (a newer one with the same tag replaces it), open (a dashboard id), actions (up to 3 buttons { label, run = function(who) ... end, roles = { "admin" } (who may press it; "admin" includes the owner), id }; run returns the text shown, or false and why), expires (seconds the buttons work, default 3600). Cloud.notify(title, body) is the short form.

Cloud.label: channel
Cloud.documentation: A channel for Calendar:notify and other code that takes an object with :send(e): each event becomes a notification with the event's title.

Cloud.label: presence
Cloud.documentation: Everyone who shares their presence with this home, sorted by name.

Cloud.label: isHome
Cloud.documentation: Whether someone is at home, by their name or cloud id.

Cloud.label: disable
Cloud.documentation: Switches the connection to the cloud off, keeping the pairing: access from away (dashboards, devices and voice through the cloud) and notifications stop until Cloud.enable() or the switch on the cloud page. The app on the home's network keeps working (up to a week without the cloud); to end that too, unpair. It is saved and survives a restart; the cloud shows the home as switched off and sends no offline alert.

Cloud.label: enable
Cloud.documentation: Switches the connection to the cloud on again, with the same pairing.

Cloud.label: enabled
Cloud.documentation: Whether vCLU is paired with the cloud and the connection is switched on.

Cloud.label: anyoneHome
Cloud.documentation: Whether anyone who shares their presence is at home (false when nobody shares it).

Cloud.label: onPresence
Cloud.documentation: Calls fn(e) when someone comes home or leaves: e = { user, name, home, since, anyone } (anyone: whether anyone is at home after this change). Runs as that person (origin "remote").

Dashboard.label: new
Dashboard.documentation: Create a new DashboardBuilder for the given ID.

Dashboard.label: dynamic
Dashboard.documentation: Register a dynamic dashboard that rebuilds on every definition request. The builder function receives a fresh DashboardBuilder and should configure it. build() is called automatically if the function doesn't call it.

Dashboard.label: periodLabel
Dashboard.documentation: Return human-friendly label for a period.

DashboardAPI.label: getAuth
DashboardAPI.documentation: Get auth type and poll interval for a dashboard (lightweight, no getValue calls)

DashboardAPI.label: remoteList
DashboardAPI.documentation: The dashboards reachable through vclu cloud, for its "dashboards" message

DashboardAPI.label: remoteCamera
DashboardAPI.documentation: Whether a camera's snapshot is on a dashboard this remote viewer sees (an image widget) :roles() against the person), nil for any remote one

DashboardAPI.label: getAppInfo
DashboardAPI.documentation: What the home-screen app of a dashboard needs: no widgets or values, any auth may read it

DashboardAPI.label: usesMetric
DashboardAPI.documentation: Whether the dashboard draws this metric (chart or status sparkline)

DashboardAPI.label: widgetHidden
DashboardAPI.documentation: Whether visible() hides the widget now: the server asks before it answers from its cache

DashboardAPI.label: calendarRange
DashboardAPI.documentation: Occurrences of a calendar widget's calendar for the days from..to ('YYYY-MM-DD', at most 42) or {error, status} with the HTTP status of a bad request

DashboardAPI.label: list
DashboardAPI.documentation: List all dashboards with widget details

DashboardAPI.label: getDefinition
DashboardAPI.documentation: Get full dashboard definition with current values

DashboardAPI.label: executeAction
DashboardAPI.detail: (id: string, widgetId: string, action: string, value: any, ctx: table|nil): string
DashboardAPI.documentation: Execute a widget action also role (the remote viewer's role) and confirmed (the person confirmed a remote = { confirm = true } button)

DashboardAPI.label: getPin
DashboardAPI.documentation: PIN of a 'pin' dashboard, for checking cookies server-side (never sent to pages)

DashboardBuilder.label: name
DashboardBuilder.detail: (s: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the display name for this dashboard.

DashboardBuilder.label: icon
DashboardBuilder.detail: (s: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the icon for this dashboard.

DashboardBuilder.label: columns
DashboardBuilder.detail: (n: number)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the number of grid columns.

DashboardBuilder.label: width
DashboardBuilder.detail: (w: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the page width: 'full' fills the screen edge to edge (wall tablets), 'normal' (default) keeps wide screens centred.

DashboardBuilder.label: auth
DashboardBuilder.detail: (s: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the authentication mode ("public", "pin").

DashboardBuilder.label: pin
DashboardBuilder.detail: (s: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the PIN code for pin-authenticated dashboards.

DashboardBuilder.label: poll
DashboardBuilder.detail: (n: number)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the poll interval in seconds. A page gets state changes at once over its WebSocket; values that no state change shows (the time, a variable) are read again every n seconds, and a page without the socket polls them that often.

DashboardBuilder.label: theme
DashboardBuilder.detail: (t: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Set the dashboard theme.

DashboardBuilder.label: tabGroup
DashboardBuilder.detail: (name: string)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add this dashboard to a named tab group for navigation.

DashboardBuilder.label: remote
DashboardBuilder.detail: (spec: boolean|table|nil)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Make the dashboard reachable through vclu cloud: :remote() (or true), :remote(false) to take it back, or a table {pin = true (remote viewers also enter the PIN), poll = seconds (default 5, at least 2)}. Every member of the home sees it, or with :roles(...) only those given one of those roles in the cloud. Without it the dashboard never leaves the house. Widgets narrow it with opts.remote: false (not sent), 'readonly', or {confirm = true}.

DashboardBuilder.label: roles
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Who sees the remote dashboard in vclu cloud: people given one of these roles there (e.g. 'domownicy', 'gosia'). The cloud decides; vCLU only passes the names on. Without it every member of the home sees it. A function instead of names decides again and again (e.g. the cleaner only on Tuesdays 9-13): it returns the roles as a table, and the cloud gets each change within about 15 s; nil, an empty table or an error hide the dashboard from everyone in the cloud.

DashboardBuilder.label: header
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Start a header section (must be called before any section).

DashboardBuilder.label: section
DashboardBuilder.detail: (name: string, icon: string, opts: table): SectionHandle
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Start a new named section for grouping widgets.

DashboardBuilder.label: floor
DashboardBuilder.detail: (floor: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add one section per area on a floor (expose(..., { area = "Salon", floor = "Parter" })), each filled as section:area; areas with nothing to show are left out. Read each time the dashboard is, so new areas show up. Start a section() to add widgets by hand after it. With rooms = true: one section named after the floor with a room tile per area (section:room).

DashboardBuilder.label: room
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, area: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a room tile to the current section (see SectionHandle:room).

DashboardBuilder.label: button
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, onTap: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a button widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: toggle
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, getValue: function, onToggle: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a toggle widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: slider
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, min: number, max: number, getValue: function, onSet: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a slider widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: status
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, getValue: function, unit: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a status widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: link
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, url: string|function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a link widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: chart
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, metricPath: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a chart widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: bars
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, metricPath: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a bar chart of a metric to the current section: one bar per hour, day, week or month of the house's zone.

DashboardBuilder.label: calendar
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, cal: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a calendar widget to the current section: a month grid and the day of a tapped date. holidays=true (holiday names, on by default), namedays=false (name days in the day view), sun=true (sunrise and sunset in the day view, with :location()), span=n, visible=function()->bool}; what is off is not sent to the browser

DashboardBuilder.label: select
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, options: table, getValue: function, onSelect: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a select widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: image
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, url: string|function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add an image widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: group
DashboardBuilder.detail: (label: string, icon: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a group label widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: cover
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, fns: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a cover widget to the current section. Buttons up/stop/down call open/stop/close. With set, a 0-100% slider is shown under them. With setTilt, a 0-90° slat slider is shown while getTilt gives a number (0 = open, 90 = closed, as in Grenton). Position 0 = closed, 100 = open, as in Grenton; nil (not reported yet) is shown as --. getState lights the button of the movement: 0 = stopped, 1 = up, 2 = down.

DashboardBuilder.label: gate
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a gate (or a door lock) to the current section: its state, Open, Close and Stop. Open and Close are pressed and held (Close shown only with close), Stop is a tap.

DashboardBuilder.label: covers
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, list: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a cover group to the current section: one tile moving several covers, with their counts and average position. Buttons up/stop/down call open/stop/close on each cover, the slider setPosition on those with a position, the slat slider (shown when a cover reports getTilt) setTilt on those with a tilt; commands go out 50 ms apart and a new movement (or slat) command drops what is left of the previous one; stop ends both.

DashboardBuilder.label: player
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, src: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a media player to the current section: artwork, title and artist, previous/play-pause/next, volume, mute and power.

DashboardBuilder.label: forecast
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, src: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a weather forecast to the current section: the next days and a chart of the next hours.

DashboardBuilder.label: table
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, rows: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a table to the current section: rows from a function, in the columns of opts.columns.

DashboardBuilder.label: energy
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add an energy flow to the current section: PV, grid, battery and home with the power between them.

DashboardBuilder.label: dimmer
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, fns: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a dimmer widget to the current section.

DashboardBuilder.label: color
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string, fns: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a color picker widget to the current section. switchOn?, switchOff?, isOn?, getWhite?/setWhite? white 0-100}, or a RemoteRGBLight (white when it has one)

DashboardBuilder.label: gauge
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, getValue: function, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a gauge to the current section: a value on an arc or a bar between min and max. style="arc" (default) is a 240° arc with the value in the middle, "bar" a horizontal bar with the value at its right; from each threshold's value on the fill takes its colour; a value outside min..max is drawn at the end, the number shows it as it is.

DashboardBuilder.label: colorTemp
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, fns: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a colour temperature slider (warm to cool white) to the current section. getBrightness?/setBrightness? 0-100}, or an object with getColorTemp/setColorTemp in kelvin (and its switchOn/switchOff/getBrightness/setBrightness when it has them); a two-channel warm/cold white: require("lib/cct").mix(warm, cold) The slider runs warm to cool over a gradient; the value shows as "3000 K" and a word (warm, neutral, cool). A set outside min..max is clamped to it; a reading outside is shown as it is. A toggle when there are switchOn and switchOff, a brightness slider when there are getBrightness and setBrightness.

DashboardBuilder.label: thermostat
DashboardBuilder.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string|nil, fns: table, opts: table)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Add a thermostat to the current section: current temperature, target and +/- for the target. getState=function()->number|bool? (1/true active, 0/false off), getMode=function()->number? (0 manual, 1 holiday, 2 schedule, 3 heat-up), setMode=function(value)? (with opts.modes)}, or a thermostat object (RemoteThermostat, VirtualThermostat: getValue, getTarget, setSetpoint, getState, getMode, setMode?) Shows the current temperature and the target ("--" until reported); + and - change the target by step and setTarget is called once, 1 s after the last tap; the chosen value shows until the thermostat reports a new target, at most 90 s. Without setTarget (or opts.readonly) there are no buttons; with getMode the target is set only in manual mode (0), as lib/panel does. The action endpoint refuses a set outside min..max. Modes: a switch under the target. A VirtualThermostat gets manual (0), holiday (1) and "off" (stop; another mode starts it again) by itself; a RemoteThermostat only shows its mode. A table of functions gets one with fns.getMode, fns.setMode and opts.modes; getMode gives one of the values, setMode(value) gets the chosen one. In a mode marked readonly (holiday) there are no + and -. opts.readonly locks the switch too.

DashboardBuilder.label: when
DashboardBuilder.detail: (periods: table|string, fn: function)
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Conditional block: only execute fn if current time matches any of the given periods.

DashboardBuilder.label: build
DashboardBuilder.documentation: Finalize and register the dashboard in the global registry.

M.detail: = 50 — Tunable white from two dimmers: a warm and a cold white channel as one colour temperature. local cct = require("lib/cct") local biuro = cct.mix(_:get("CLU1.DIM1"), _:get("CLU1.DIM2"), { warm = 2700, cold = 6500 }) dash:section("Biuro"):colorTemp("biuro", "Biuro", biuro, { min = 2700, max = 6500 }) A channel is anything with getValue/setValue on 0..1 (RemoteLight, RemoteLedChannel, VirtualDimmer). Brightness is the sum of both channels (at most 100%), the colour temperature their ratio, linear in kelvin between warm and cold. Changing one keeps the other. A colour temperature set while both are off is kept for the next switchOn, and so are the level and colour temperature a light had before it was switched off (also by a scene or a wall switch, when a poll saw them). While the channels show what the mix sent (within one 0..255 step) it keeps its own kelvin: a dim light on stepped channels does not drift. Commands go out at least 50 ms apart, only the latest values wait: the CLU drops bursts (pkg/lua/AGENTS.md).

Panel.detail: = 15 — Panel: vCLU runs a Grenton Smart Panel. The CLU only forwards the panel's events (click(name, input)); this library keeps the state (open pages, cursor, edits, idle timer) and draws the screen with frames sent by RemotePanel. The panel is a square with four buttons in the corners around a small display: a page gives the corners meanings (roles up, down, ok); one corner is always back. Hints for the corners are drawn next to them, the buttons' LEDs show which work. local Panel = require("lib/panel") Panel.new(dom.P1_PANEL_SALON) :home(Panel.menu("Dom") :toggle("Swiatlo", dom.LAMPA) :number("Zadana", getFn, setFn, { step = 0.5, min = 19, max = 22 })) :idle(Panel.idle{ { "Salon", dom.TEMP } }) :sleepAfter(30) A page is a table: draw(screen, panel), keys (table or function(panel) -> {role = {label, fn}}), input(name, panel), back(panel) -> true when it handled back itself, watch (objects or function), every (seconds), modal (gets every input, no hints), open/close(panel). Panel.register(name, factory) adds a page type as Panel.<name>. Screen layout (128 x 64). Measured on a Smart Panel WiFi (module fv05): y is the top of the text; font 1 is 10 px high (capitals; g, y go lower), font 2 14 px, font 3 28 px. PrintText paints a black cell behind every letter, so text never inverts and nothing fills a box (DrawBox draws nothing): every frame redraws the whole screen. The fonts are proportional: a row holds 16 digits in font 1 and 13 in font 2; a space is narrower (about 6 px), so a column is set by x, never by leading spaces. narrower characters in font 1 (measured from a photo); other fonts scale them by cw

SectionHandle.label: new
SectionHandle.documentation: Dashboard - Lua-defined dashboards for tablet/wall-mounted control panels Builder pattern API for defining dashboards entirely in Lua. Each dashboard is a public page at /d/:id with per-dashboard auth. Global registry (cleared on module reload, rebuilt by build() calls) ========================================================================== SectionHandle - proxy for adding widgets to a specific section ========================================================================== "a", "b": the sorted keys of a set, or "none". :width() of a dashboard; level points the error at the module's line ========================================================================== Press and hold: opts.hold on a button, a toggle and a gate ========================================================================== opts.hold in ms (true = 800, 300-5000), nil without; dflt is a gate's default (true) A button or a toggle: its hold checked when it is added, so a mistake fails the module ========================================================================== Gate (or a lock): its state, open/close held, stop at a tap ========================================================================== What the tile shows: {state} (none while state gives nil or is not given), or {error} A calendar widget keeps the calendar's id, so a dashboard may be built before the calendar. a calendar built already (the usual order: its module, then the dashboard) is checked now A colour widget given a light object (RemoteRGBLight) instead of fns. Reads come from what the light keeps (a get() would ask the CLU on every poll); brightness and white are 0..100. ========================================================================== Cover groups: one tile for several covers ========================================================================== Spacing between commands of one series: the CLU drops bursts (pkg/lua/AGENTS.md) A cover object: a table with the three moves (RemoteCover, VirtualCover) Problems with a cover list already logged, by "dashboard/widget/what" The covers of a group as they are now: a function list is called, paths looked up; missing ones skipped opts.decimals of a status: whole places 0..6; the page rounds a number to them ========================================================================== Bars: a metric summed, averaged... per hour or day of the house's zone ========================================================================== "7d", "24h", "90m", "1h30m" -> seconds, nil when it is not a duration ========================================================================== Chart: a metric over a range, or over ranges the viewer switches between ========================================================================== ========================================================================== Thermostat: current temperature, target, +/- for the target ========================================================================== a map's well-known names in this order, the others after them A-Z the range of an exposed climate (ExposedObjects capabilities) A thermostat object, as Home Assistant's climate takes one (RemoteThermostat) An error value as text; tostring itself may fail (a bad __tostring) The object's methods as the widget's functions; as lib/panel's menu:thermostat, the set point is written by hand, so only in manual mode (getMode 0) The modes an object switches itself (VirtualThermostat): set point and holiday by setMode, "off" by stop when it has start/stop; nil without setMode (a RemoteThermostat only reports its mode) a mode chosen while stopped starts it again opts.modes as a list of {value, label, icon?, readonly?}: a list as given, a map {value = label} ordered by value (numbers, then manual, schedule, holiday, off, then A-Z) a list starts with a table; {[0] = "Ręczny", [1] = "Urlop"} is a map the object's modes under the module's labels and order an object (it has methods), but not a thermostat: say which and what it lacks; a table of functions with a metatable (own getCurrent) stays a table of functions a readonly function locks and unlocks the buttons while the dashboard runs; readonly = true keeps the modes for the state line, without the switch A finite number from fn, nil before the first report; err when fn fails opts.readonly as a function: true (or failing) locks the target and the modes The mode the switch shows: a number or a string, nil before a report; err when getMode fails The target may be written: there is setTarget, nothing locks it and the mode allows it: with modes one not marked readonly (one not in the list does not); an object's own mode manual (0, or not known yet), also while it is off; a failing getMode or readonly says no What the tile shows: {current, target, state, mode, set}, error when getCurrent or getTarget fails false, not nil: the page merges values, so a missing field would keep the last true ========================================================================== Gauge: a value on an arc or a bar between min and max ========================================================================== A colour the page can use as is: a name it knows, #hex, rgb()/hsl() A decimal numeral ("12", "-3.5", ".5"), not hex or other forms tonumber takes Target functions that failed, logged once by "dashboard/widget" What the tile shows: {value, target, error}; nil is left out (a poll is the whole state, the page reads a missing field as none), error when getValue fails or gives what is not a number ========================================================================== Colour temperature: a warm-to-cool slider in kelvin ========================================================================== A number, or a string of decimal digits ("3000", not "0x10"); nil otherwise An object with getColorTemp/setColorTemp (kelvin) as the widget's functions; the rest when it has them opts.unit = "mired": the functions speak mireds, the widget kelvin (1e6 / x, rounded) What the tile shows: {kelvin, on, brightness}; a failing function gives error, nothing else a reading out of min..max is shown as it is; the slider stops at its end ========================================================================== Rooms from the house model (section:area, dash:floor) ========================================================================== Kinds that have a widget; a thermostat (climate) only through kinds, as switch and lock Checked options of section:area / dash:floor; errors name the module's line (level) Paths already warned about: dashboard = true on a kind without a widget A widget for an exposed object, or nil for a kind without one; off() also disables it (a room tile's) a pulse switch (a gate) pulses through its handle, never stays on a Grenton roller keeps its movement aside; without a position the state is the movement the expose options' range, as Home Assistant clamps a target; readonly disables the widget A path in an id: other bytes as %XX, so two paths never give one id base, or base#2, #3... when taken Widgets of the devices in areas (on floor, when given); ids from the path, the same on every read; "#n" only for the same device shown again Temperature and humidity devices of a room (dashboard = false and skip leave them out) Tilt only where the object has both methods and reports an angle A cover with a position (a Grenton roller without one has _hasPosition = false) Counts of covers by state; not moving and no position is unknown What a group tile shows: counts, the average position and tilt, whether a slider can set them Series of commands by "dashboard/widget/move" and ".../tilt": the first now, the next ones COVERS_SPACING_MS apart on timers; a new one of the same kind drops what is left of the old stopIf() true before a later step (the widget got disabled) drops the rest ========================================================================== Media player: artwork, title, artist, transport and volume ========================================================================== A MusicCast device (@vclu/musiccast) by its methods, not the plugin's internals The device's methods as the player's functions; its getState mapped to the tile's the device's methods take an optional callback after their arguments The controls the functions allow; a missing one hides its button Text for the page: a string or a number, cut to a sane length (not mid-character) drop a last UTF-8 character the cut left incomplete The page sets it as an src: only an absolute http(s) URL What the tile shows: {playing, title, artist, album, artwork, volume, muted, power, online}, or {error} ========================================================================== Weather forecast: the next days and a chart of the next hours ========================================================================== the Weather plugin (@vclu/weather): its getForecast gives the same table A finite number rounded to one decimal, or nil A Bootstrap icon name from the data; anything else is a cloud What the tile shows: {days, hours, updated}, {none = true} before the first fetch, or {error} 0..1 is a fraction; above 1 it is a percent already the current hour and limit-1 after it: exactly limit points of hourly data ========================================================================== Table: rows from a function, columns from opts ========================================================================== rows sent to the page at most, whatever limit says ========================================================================== Energy flow: PV, grid, battery and home with the power between them ========================================================================== the lines between nodes; a positive power flows from the first to the second A reading as a finite number (a decimal string counts, "1,5" too), nil without one, or nil and the error What the tile shows: each node's power in W ({power}, {none} or {error}), the battery's SoC, the power on each line between nodes, and the kWh of today PV without a reading (an inverter asleep at night) counts as 0; an error does not home from the balance, unknown when grid or battery is PV goes to the battery first, then out to the grid, the rest to the home; a discharging battery feeds the home, what it gives beyond that goes to the grid a measured home: the lines into it scaled to what it takes a line exists between two nodes; it carries a power only when both are read grid_battery goes both ways: below zero the battery feeds the grid The dashboard as the API reads it: area sections filled from what is exposed, a floor one section per area (or one of room tiles); reused until something is exposed, unexposed or its options change (widgets read the objects live). A room tile's overlay is a hidden section after the visible ones, so its widgets go through values and actions like any other. the tile with what it counts; ids of its overlay are given after the visible sections' section:group's options: a table with visible only; level as error()'s

Numbers are rounded to the column's decimals, booleans show as ✓ and —, nil as an empty cell; a header tap sorts on the page; on a phone each row is a card. rows must be a list (1..n, no holes); the first 1000 are read and sorted, at most 200 go to the page.

SectionHandle.label: energy
SectionHandle.detail: (id: string, label: string, opts: table)
SectionHandle.documentation: Add an energy flow: PV, grid, battery and home as nodes, with the power flowing between them. Each function returns the power now (W, or kW with unit="kW"), nil while there is no reading; pv is 0 or more, grid is + taken from the grid and - given to it, battery + charging and - discharging (invert flips one that counts the other way). A node without its function is left out (a house without a battery); home without one is pv + grid - battery, at least 0 (PV without a reading counts as 0). A function that fails shows "—" on its node, the rest of the tile stays.

SectionHandle.label: colorTemp
SectionHandle.detail: (id: string, label: string, fns: table, opts: table)
SectionHandle.documentation: Add a colour temperature slider (warm to cool white) to this section. getBrightness?/setBrightness? 0-100}, or an object with getColorTemp/setColorTemp in kelvin (and its switchOn/switchOff/getBrightness/setBrightness when it has them); a two-channel warm/cold white: require("lib/cct").mix(warm, cold) The slider runs warm to cool over a gradient; the value shows as "3000 K" and a word (warm, neutral, cool). A set outside min..max is clamped to it; a reading outside is shown as it is. A toggle when there are switchOn and switchOff, a brightness slider when there are getBrightness and setBrightness.

SectionHandle.label: thermostat
SectionHandle.detail: (id: string, label: string, icon: string|nil, fns: table, opts: table)
SectionHandle.documentation: Add a thermostat: current temperature, target and +/- for the target. getState=function()->number|bool? (1/true active, 0/false off), getMode=function()->number? (0 manual, 1 holiday, 2 schedule, 3 heat-up), setMode=function(value)? (with opts.modes)}, or a thermostat object (RemoteThermostat, VirtualThermostat: getValue, getTarget, setSetpoint, getState, getMode, setMode?) Shows the current temperature and the target ("--" until reported); + and - change the target by step and setTarget is called once, 1 s after the last tap; the chosen value shows until the thermostat reports a new target, at most 90 s. Without setTarget (or opts.readonly) there are no buttons; with getMode the target is set only in manual mode (0), as lib/panel does. The action endpoint refuses a set outside min..max. Modes: a switch under the target. A VirtualThermostat gets manual (0), holiday (1) and "off" (stop; another mode starts it again) by itself; a RemoteThermostat only shows its mode. A table of functions gets one with fns.getMode, fns.setMode and opts.modes; getMode gives one of the values, setMode(value) gets the chosen one. In a mode marked readonly (holiday) there are no + and -. opts.readonly locks the switch too.

SectionHandle.label: gauge
SectionHandle.detail: (id: string, label: string, getValue: function, opts: table)
SectionHandle.documentation: Add a gauge: a value on an arc or a bar between min and max, coloured by thresholds. style="arc" (default) is a 240° arc with the value in the middle, "bar" a horizontal bar with the value at its right; from each threshold's value on the fill takes its colour; a value outside min..max is drawn at the end, the number shows it as it is.

SectionHandle.label: chip

SectionHandle.label: area
SectionHandle.detail: (area: string, opts: table)
SectionHandle.documentation: Fill this section with a widget for every device expose() put in an area, picked by kind: a light, switch or lock a toggle, a dimmer a dimmer, an RGB light the colour widget, a light with getColorTemp/setColorTemp the colour temperature (2700-6500 K), a cover a cover, temperature and humidity a status; lights first, then covers, then the rest by name. Filled when something is exposed or unexposed, so devices a plugin exposes later show up; widgets added by hand come after them; a read-only device's widget is disabled. Like the panel, expose(obj, type, { dashboard = false }) keeps an object off dashboards and dashboard = true puts one of those kinds on them even when kinds leaves it out (other kinds have no widget and log a warning). Widget ids are "area:" .. path, other bytes as %XX. Anyone who can open the dashboard controls what is exposed in the area later: use :auth('session') or 'pin'; access profiles of MQTT, HomeKit and MCP do not apply here.

Lights, dimmers and switches count as on above 0, covers as open above 0 or while moving; only what the room shows is counted. StateChange.label: filter

VirtualPresence.label: new
VirtualPresence.documentation: Creates a presence that is on while a `trigger` source is active, or a `keep` source is active after a start, or the `door` is closed with someone inside, and for `hold` seconds after the last of these ends. It starts empty (also after a restart or a reload): a trigger active at creation counts once it has changed. Options: trigger (list of objects or registry paths; 1 or true starts and keeps presence), keep (list; keeps presence that is on, never starts it), door (one object or path, 1 = open: it keeps presence until it opens once someone is seen inside after it closed: a trigger going on, or one on at closing still on doorGrace s later; closing it on leaving lets the hold run out), doorGrace (10 s: a detector that stays on longer by itself belongs in keep, or needs more), hold (300 s). Sources need getValue() (Grenton, virtual, Satel, GPIO objects); a plugin sensor has get(), so bridge it: s:onChange(function(v) vs:updateState(v) end) with vs a VirtualSensor. Do not make a light switched by this presence its own keep source.

VirtualPresence.label: set
VirtualPresence.documentation: Presence is set by its sources only: nothing is settable by index.

VirtualPresence.label: getReason
VirtualPresence.documentation: What holds presence now: "trigger: <path>", "keep: <path>", "door", "hold 42 s", "override", nil when empty.

VirtualPresence.label: getRemaining
VirtualPresence.documentation: Seconds of hold left: 0 while a source or an override holds it, or when empty.

VirtualPresence.label: getDuration
VirtualPresence.documentation: Seconds since presence started, 0 when empty.

VirtualPresence.label: trigger
VirtualPresence.documentation: A signal from code ("I'm here"): starts presence or extends it by sec (default hold). Ignored while an override is set.

VirtualPresence.label: setOverride
VirtualPresence.documentation: Forces presence: 1 present (guests), 0 empty (alarm armed), nil back to the sensors (a presence that was on then holds for hold seconds unless a source keeps it).

VirtualPresence.label: setHold
VirtualPresence.documentation: Sets the hold time; a hold already running keeps its end.

VirtualThermostat.label: new
VirtualThermostat.documentation: Creates a thermostat that switches `output` by the temperature of `source`. The output is switched off at once (also after a restart or a reload) and goes on only on a reading that arrives after; the source's value at creation does not count. Options: source (object with getValue, or its path), output (object with switchOn and switchOff, or its path), hysteresis (0.5 °C), direction ("heat" or "cool"), setpoint (21), holiday (16 heating, 28 cooling), min (5), max (35), staleAfter (900 s without a change of the source's value: output off), maxOn (s on in one go, then off until a setting changes; default no limit), lease (s >= 30, a Grenton DOUT or dimmer only: switched on for that long and renewed, so the CLU switches it off when vCLU stops), persist (true or a key: set point, mode and state survive restarts). Comfort control, not a safety device: what each failure does is in docs/ai/examples.md, "What happens when".

VirtualThermostat.label: set
VirtualThermostat.documentation: Index 0 is the temperature, which only the source sets: nothing is settable by index.

VirtualThermostat.label: getValue

VirtualThermostat.label: getTarget

VirtualThermostat.label: getSetpoint

VirtualThermostat.label: setSetpoint

VirtualThermostat.label: getState

VirtualThermostat.label: getMode

VirtualThermostat.label: setMode

VirtualThermostat.label: stop

VirtualThermostat.label: getFault

VirtualThermostat.label: getDirection
VirtualThermostat.documentation: What the output does: "heat" or "cool" (Home Assistant shows it as the mode).
